title: Enhancing Time Series Momentum Strategies Using Deep Neural Networks

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper introduces Deep Momentum Networks (DMNs), a hybrid approach that integrates deep learning-based trading rules within a volatility-scaled time series momentum framework. The models simultaneously learn trend estimation and position sizing in a data-driven manner by directly optimising performance objectives such as the Sharpe ratio via automatic differentiation. Out-of-sample performance is tested on a portfolio of 88 ratio-adjusted continuous futures contracts using a 5-year rolling recalibration scheme.
extraction.universe: 88 ratio-adjusted continuous futures contracts across commodities, fixed income, and currency futures from the Pinnacle Data Corp CLC Database

performance_metrics.context: LSTM Sharpe-optimised rescaled to target volatility
Sgn(Returns) benchmark rescaled to target volatility

key_findings: Sharpe-optimised LSTMs significantly outperform traditional time series momentum benchmarks, more than doubling the Sharpe ratio in the absence of transaction costs.
Models that directly generate positions through end-to-end Sharpe ratio optimisation perform better than standard supervised learning approaches (regression and classification).
Volatility scaling plays a crucial role in enhancing the performance of machine learning momentum models.
Machine learning models trade significantly more than traditional benchmarks, but Sharpe-optimised LSTMs remain competitive when considering transaction costs up to 2-3 basis points.
limitations: Higher strategy turnover in deep learning models leads to higher vulnerability to transaction costs compared to traditional benchmarks.
Complex architectures like WaveNet underperformed simpler linear models and LSTMs, pointing to challenges in hyperparameter tuning.
